Perfume rating 4.06 out of 5 with 7,073 votes

Narciso by Narciso Rodriguez is a Floral Woody Musk fragrance for women. Narciso was launched in 2014. The nose behind this fragrance is Aurélien Guichard. Top notes are Gardenia and White Rose; middle note is Musk; base notes are White Cedar Extract, Cedar and Vetiver.

Fashion designer Narciso Rodriguez became celebrated in the world of perfumes with his debut Narciso Rodriguez For Her from 2003. That minimalist name and design, as well as musky sensuality adorn his latest olfactory creation that comes out in September of 2014—feminine fragrance Narciso Eau de Parfum.

"I wanted to create an extremely sexy fragrance that would turn a man’s head,” announces the designer, with the description, “The sensuality becomes a little bit more sexy, a little bit more intoxicating.”

The composition is composed of white gardenia and rose above the warm heart of musk. The base includes woody accords of vetiver and two types of cedar: black and white.

The bottle is simple: square, milky white with the name printed in black letters. The face of the perfume is a model Raquel Zimmermann.

Goldena35 03/06/25 16:52

I am so happy to have added this in my collection! I am a huge fan of Narciso for Her (OG) and their signature musk in general. I only recently came around to liking Gardenia in the past few years. I read about this being d/cd and debated buying it …finally pulling the trigger on a good deal. I am beyond glad that I did. This is the softest creamy gardenia with the NR musk base mixed with beautiful grounding wood notes. It starts off a little sharp, but that fades fairly quickly and all the notes combine to create this blanket of soft, comforting, hazy goodness (gardenia and musk take the lead for me). It feels akin to being covered in a thick luxury cream. The gardenia is so soft and accented beautifully by the delicate rose (which is barely perceptible unless you are looking for it). Again the cedar can read a bit sharp initially, but once it drys down it gives this perfume needed structure. There is something that brings a touch of sweetness that *almost* reads like vanilla …but it’s not. If you think this sounds like something you would like, I urge you to buy a bottle before the prices skyrocket. I do not regret it for a second. Great perfume for everyday wear …feminine soft and creamy florals with a touch of sexy from the addicting NR musk and a powdered wood base. Stunning! (Even the bottle is gorgeous!)

Skylakagetis 11/21/24 03:23

Narciso white cube is one of my favourite ever scents, I'm heartbroken it got discontinued. I understand why but I so hope they decide to reformulate it in line with modern regulations, it really is a masterpiece of perfumery. I think if you like it, you will love it, but I can see that it can be difficult to love in the beginning because of it's sharpness. It's worth the effort to learn to love it though.

Everything about it is perfection, the gardenia and rose are very delicate but creamy and sharp. The gardenia is earthy and green, the white rose is light and delicate. The musk is absolutely beautiful, very sensual, deep, sexy and skin like. The vetiver and cedar add a glorious depth and warmth to the sharpness. The dry down is very lotiony and when I shower at night before bed, it is still there after 10+ hours, and the steam from the shower releases the most sensual lotiony, warm skin like musk ever, I LOVE it. It's one of those fragrances that makes my eyes roll into the back of my head when I smell it!

I only get the white rose note in the inside of my elbow, not really anywhere else. I assume this is because the skin there is more protected from evaporation and has less air exposure.

I think the cedar notes come from Iso E Super, I pick this up in the woodiness and if I layer Molecule 01 with this, it doesn't change the perfume in any way, it only boosts it - so I think it must have this within the composition already. When I layer with other scents I usually pick up on subtle changes but not here.

The musk in Narciso does a very good job at being on the cusp of "dirty", it's just on the edge of that it is clean or is it dirty? I think it smells like warm, sensual and sexy skin, wearing a delicate and expensive floral lotion. Narciso smells expensive and well made. Every part of it is intentional.

This isn't sweet, it's mostly sharp, creamy and woody but as it dries down it gets slightly softer , lotiony and almost sweet, but not quite!

Narciso has incredible longevity but does drop to a skin scent for me after a few hours. Longevity is excellent but definitely doesn't project that much on me. I often get compliments on this perfume from people close to me. I've never smelled it on anyone else that I am aware of.

The opening of Poudree is very similar to this but it's much warmer and sweeter in its heart and base. It reminds me a lot of a very floral musky Hypnotic Poison in its dry down. They are not similar really during wear apart from a resemblance in their openings.

I find this very different to the Rouge EDP and EDT, they are makeuppy powdery scents.

Wristsniffer 08/12/24 22:21

There's really nothing like this. I wish I had stockpiled it a couple of years ago when it was discontinued. That said, the fact that this is so rare makes it even that much more precious. I save it for cashmere days and dress up evenings.

I was a huge fan of Rush back in the day, and I remember the addictive nature of it. When I read Luca Turin's review of Narciso, I'd already fallen for it and purchased a big bottle without realizing it shared a lactonic accord with Rush. There's something about that milky note combined with something slightly sour (in both Rush and Narciso there's a lot of vetiver - a favorite sour note of mine) that really is addictive. This is what sets the EDP apart from Poudree and subsequent flankers, and what makes its discontinuation so tragic. Though, some of its ingredients are now banned so I have to respect them for pulling it instead of attempting to reformulate.

The best way I can describe Narciso is as a seamless, fuzzy velvet - almost leathery but in texture only, not as a note. You're not distinctly aware of smelling gardenia, or rose, or cedar, or musk, or vetiver, or amber, but they're all there. The first few hours are undeniably gorgeous - a thick, rich, decadent dichotomy of dark and light notes which somehow create an harmonious dischord. Narciso gets sweeter and more powdery as it dries down. It doesn't last for ages on my skin, but I get several hours of intense wear, followed by a couple of hours as a skin scent. It lasts slightly longer in warmer weather, which is my favorite time to wear this.

I have the perfume oil version of this as well, and while it's absolutely lovely, it is softer and I do prefer the EDP. I blind bought Narciso Rouge and sadly, was mostly anosmic to it. I have a travel size of the EDT which came in a set. It's pretty, but very different from the EDP, and I never felt compelled to buy a bigger bottle. I enjoyed Poudree but found it too similar in structure to the original to justify both, and lacking in the sour milkiness I love in the EDP. It also turned a bit bitter on my skin (coumarin does that to me), but when I sprayed it on my clothes it was fine. I may buy a bottle at some point as it's quite beautiful, it's just not the original. I've yet to try Ambree or Cristal, as the reviews didn't convince me I'd be enamored.

I'd love to see Narciso bring Aurelien Guichard back in to do another version of the line with compliant ingredients - something akin to this original beauty but maybe an intense version as a 10 year anniversary limited edition or something. When I get to the last bit of my bottle I will not use it. I need to be able to at least smell this in the bottle until the day I die haha. It really is that good!

So here is my comparison: Initial spray is a bit different, Vivian seems to be a bit harsher, but this harshness fades quickly. Narciso has this balsamic, milky creamy undertone from the early dry down, from the first hour or so. The Verset version gets to this stage only after 3-4 hours. While waiting for the Verset's dry down, I could tell them apart, Vivian was fresher, more powdery, and the rosy aspect came forward a little bit more. I thought that this will be the main difference, but no, just Vivian dries down much slower. While Narciso disappeared from my skin after 5 hours, Vivan stayed for 8, until I had a shower, but she was still present quite strongly. I have to say I was very surprised, because in sum, I found that the Verset version is better quality. Staying power is better and a bit stronger. Hope they don't reformulate.

There is this one person you always run into when you visit the park. You smile at them every time you cross paths, and you decide maybe the next time I see them, I'll just say "hi" and see if we connect. You indirectly ask other people who know them, and they tell you what you already know. You get on the internet and start looking up their name, and you look for them but this other person looking like them shows up. Now you are confused. What if it is the wrong person? And then one fine day, while looking them up, they show up in your searches and you go get them!

This was exactly how I could snag one of the last bottles. Frabra88 04/26/23 10:37

Why is it no longer with us? Oh, why?
This was one of the first perfumes that made me think "there is more to it" in this hobby of mine. I understood, then, that perfumery can be art.

This is the scent of a fallen angel...the smell of the graces of heven still lingering on his wings, milky snowy gardenia and sweetened tender white rose....but he has acquired a sensual and sexual nature now, rendered through the musk; pulsating, animalic but still clean. Addictive warm profound musk. Capable of dulling the senses.
The angel has dirt on him, the earthy vetiver and the smell of the woods of the forest in wich now resides, alone. Some of the more cold and somber facets of the gardenia still there...conveing his lonliness.
The dreams of paradise ever haunt him but he is ready now to bask himself in his newly found human sensuality and vulnerability.

This perfume has grace, delicacy, cleanleness, romanticism, but also eroticism, sensuality and warmness all in one. Everything, from the flowers to the musk to the woods are exceptional; the white cedar extract is humid and almost lactonic, and paired with that innocent yet "cruel" gardenia made for one of the most beautiful and touching "white" accord ever.
It follows you everywhere and the musk and woods become a second skin. The opening has a particular effect, the florals made me think of white and pink lace and powder, but then they change in to something mature and detached.
The person who wears this is elegant, complex and unforgettable.

The scent fitted the brand's "high fashion bareness" quite well.
The ads were some of the best imagery since Calvin Klein's Obsession, in terms of how the scent pairs with the visuals.
The Narciso woman is a vulnerable, sensual, grounded creature.

The packaging was well chosen, and the prodouct's price fair considered the quality.
I wish the Narciso Rodriguez team could find in his heart the strenght to give this back to us. A reformulation should not be so difficoult with all the new well perfoming lilial substitutes.

I understand infact that this was discontinued because it had lilial in it and removed from shops for safety reasons.
I managed to buy a 50ml for an honest price (67,00 €) together with the Narciso Rodriguez Narciso edt, black cube version with transparent cap. I am even tempted to buy more (I scavengered every reputable italian online shop and found a few).
My new bottle is from 2015, I can't quite decide if it is a little turned because the opening is somewhat sour...a sort of hair spray effect, and more earthy. Instead the bottle I had left to macerate for years has a potent floral round smell in the opening, never smelled something so beautiful, and the musk multiplied its hot effect!!! The liquid a vivid pink. I am leaving my new bottle alone to do the same.

This is not comparable too much to his flankers other then the black cube Narciso edt...Narciso Poudree, very beautiful in iteself, is less woody, more tonka sweet, a powder bomb, the florals in it are another thing, so very different. The dna they share is through the body of musk (which I read was a mix of different musks materials united to recreate the egyptian black musk dear to Msr. Narciso Rodriguez). The same consideration can be made about Narciso Rouge edp, very make-upy, another love of mine.
The one more close to it is the Narciso Rouge edt (the one with red cube pack and transparent cap), since it has the same musk and woodiness/earthiness but still...the florals/muguet in it give a different vibe.
Narciso Neroli and Neroli Ambree start to deviate even further, with a more seasoned base; the new Narciso Cristal is not even a flanker anymore.
For even more references in the Rodriguez line, all the Narciso For Her line I find very different, they don't even share the same type of musk, there it is a little more dirty.
At the same time I must say that the house of Narciso Rodriguez has a very distinct identity and personality, dna is surely shared between all his offerings.
You could blind smell all of them and you would know they are Narciso Rodriguez. I feel it is worthy of respect when a house manages to do that without being redundant.

If I can finish this long review with a word of advice then I would suggest to everyone to give a chance to their men perfumes too; most of them are unisex and incredible, smell just like an androgynous angel! There is an aura of unattainable elegance and refinement about them, and many share the same clean yet carnal musk.

kittywhiskers 09/20/22 16:51

I truly have a love/hate relationship with this fragrance. Possibly because I attempted to wear it in the summer heat one year, and it just made me feel so nauseous - this scent is way too heavy for warm weather. The first time I ever smelled it, I sprayed it on my wrist at Sephora in the dead middle of winter. After leaving the store and walking around downtown in the cool, dry air, I couldn't stop myself from sniffing my wrist every thirty seconds, craving more and more of this musky, white floral scent.

After telling myself time and time again that I really do not need another full-size bottle of perfume, I ended up buying the gift set online, which came with shower gel, body lotion and a 90ml bottle. Back in 2017, I used this nearly every day from January to May, which is around the time I met my boyfriend, so this scent definitely brings up some good memories of our early days. It was June of that year that I mistakenly, stupidly, wore it when it was hot and humid out, and from then on I could barely get a whiff of it without getting a headache, for the past 4 years.

Fast forward to today, when I decided to give her another try, as it's a cold, rainy day and I'm stuck in bed with gastro, can't get any sicker so might as well give her another try! She meant so much to me! Lo and behold, she has found her way back into my current rotation. This fragrance is mostly linear to me, there is nothing too complex about it, but sometimes simplicity can be a great thing. Upon first spray, I do get the perfect blend of gardenia and rose. There's a cloud of powder enveloping them too. They continue to linger in the background as musk and cedar come into play moments later, and I feel as though I'm in a dense forest with those flowers at my feet. I just close my eyes and drift into a creamy, woody paradise. The powder stays for the whole show.

One spray is all you need for this one to last all day. Any more than 2 sprays could be headache inducing. It's a good everyday perfume, suitable for the office if you spray lightly. The sillage is impeccable; I've gotten compliments on it from people standing 12 ft away. So disappointed to find out this has been discontinued, because it seems to be so popular. I'll be using it sparingly, and can't wait to try other Narciso perfumes.

This beauty is one of my favourite fragrances. It is a beautifully simple smelling fragrance. Narciso Rodriques know what they are doing with musks, especially clean musks. Narciso is a beautiful,clean, musky, powdery scent. The florals are smooth and creamy. The musk is soft and fluffy and the woods contribute a soft bite. It's a fairly mature and feminine fragrance. I'm not sure a lot of very young women will find this appealing. I see it attracting the 30+ crowd. I've worn it in all seasons, but not on a very hot, humid summer day. I'm nervous to try it in high heat, but a warm summer day it smells lovely.

Narciso has amazing performance. it lasts all day, 12+ hours. The scent floats around me all day and leaves a beautiful sillage. The projection is quite good, a couple of meters. I find I only need 2-4 sprays for great performance. partly because the atomiser is on the generous side and dispenses the juice in a wide fine mist.

The only fragrance that I have tried that smells similar to Narciso (other than it's flankers) is Cartier La Panthere. Panthere has a lot more sweetness and is less clean (more animalic). The drydown is where they are most similar to me. I have the EDP flankers of Narciso and really enjoy them all, especially Poudree, I think I love it just as much.
I love the classy simplicity of the bottle. It suits the fragrance perfectly.

Photojenchick 02/01/15 23:03

Abstract, synthetic and beautiful. Narciso resonates as a skin scent for hours on end, becoming a part of the wearer. It's rare to encounter a fragrance that blurs the boundaries so artfully between the frangrance wearing you and you wearing the fragrance. It yields a quiet but substantial radiation that is more likely to yield comments from others in the vein of, "You smell wonderful," not, "What are you wearing?" There is a difference.

Based on how the fragrance mingled with my skin and NR's own press release description regarding the use of cedar, I suspect there's moderate to heavy use of Iso E Super at play. In fact, after ~ 4 hours of my skin, the fragrance's drydown had morphed into a near note-for-note rendition of that of Cartier's Declaration, albeit with a more feminine facet thanks to the most abstract gardenia note likely ever orchistrated.

Synthetic and abstract are not usually synonymous with all things lovely, astounding, and perfect, but in this instance, they are. Narciso is startlingly, hauntingly beautiful.

That said, a caution: Please try before you buy. If blurry, halo-effect, resonating scents sound like a one-way ticket to migraine-ville, do not think of going here without sampling first, especially if you're sensitive to Iso E Super. And if you've tried Escentric's Molecule 01 and could smell nothing, then def try before you buy. Gorgeous bottle or not (and photos do not do this one justice), Narciso is simply not worth it if you can't smell it. I, for one, can and am so much the better for it.
